reason: The text contains multiple named characters who are not leaders. Jacob (יַעֲקֹב) is named but functions as a father seeking sustenance, not a leader. His sons—Reuben (רְאוּבֵן), Judah (יְהוּדָה), Simeon (שִׁמְעוֹן), and Benjamin (בִּנְיָמִן)—are all named characters but hold no formal leadership positions; they are servants traveling to Egypt for grain. While Joseph (יוֹסֵף) and Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה) are indeed named leaders, the presence of named non-leaders (especially the brothers and Jacob) falsifies the claim that only leaders are named.
